items.line: Unusual Whales says Bloomington, Indiana, has banned artificial superintelligence, with a 7-0 council vote, fines for violators, and a repeal bar of more than 95 percent of registered voters. A local paper confirms the vote but describes the ban's end differently; see the story.

Kasey Funderburg posts a 40-second video and says one corgi in the Carolina Panthers corgi race "decided to go rogue" and was taken down by a group effort. The video has no description, so what it shows is not checked here.

Kalshi Film, an account of the prediction market Kalshi, says Amazon MGM Studios has reached the final stages of casting the next James Bond. It lists current odds: Callum Turner 37%, Josh O'Connor 32%, Robert Pattinson 29%, Jack Lowden 22%. The casting claim is not checked here.

Pirat_Nation says former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden argues the PS6 does not need more power and that Sony should instead make a $300 console rather than one that could cost $1,200. Not checked here.

Reuters reports loud booms in Riyadh, the Saudi capital, after an early warning alert. A second post says Reuters reported that Civil Defense later said the danger had passed. A third says the Energy Ministry reported no casualties after missile debris hit an Aramco building. Not checked here.
Variety posts a video of ROSÉ performing "Number One Girl" at the LACMA Art+Film Gala.

Rob Henderson, a writer, posts a quote he attributes to comedian Dave Chappelle at a Madison Square Garden show, a remark about being glad Charlie Kirk was killed. Other accounts post different wording of the same line. Not checked here.
NBC’s Saturday Night Live account posts a video of Druski’s monologue. The post says nothing more.

Turbine Traveller, an aviation account, says an Air France A350 and an American Airlines A321 turned onto conflicting paths after leaving Los Angeles airport on Saturday, and that controllers told both to turn away. It says they reportedly came within 400 feet vertically. Not checked here.

NFL reporter Ian Rapoport says Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has told teammates he plans to return later this season, with the message "Just stay alive." The post links his story, which cites sources. Not checked here.

Gianl1974 says ICE agents reportedly blocked the emergency entrance of a Los Angeles hospital for two hours and ambulances had to go elsewhere. The post gives no source for the report. Not checked here.
Pop Base, a pop culture account, posts two photos and says Taylor Swift was at today’s Chiefs game with Karlie Kloss. The photos have no description, so what they show is not checked here.

The Stalwart quotes a Bloomberg report that Nvidia’s board is investigating whether chief executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign espionage plot, after he told employees he was unfaithful to his wife. Not checked here.

Aaron Rupar posts what he says is full footage of Attorney General Todd Blanche on CNN, and calls it a “crashout.” He says Blanche confirms he will investigate Democrats on Trump’s demand and leaves open trying to imprison them. I could not see the video here. Not checked here.
Watcher Guru says $1 billion was liquidated from the crypto market in 10 minutes, with Bitcoin falling under $74,000 and Ether under $2,125. The four photos have no description. Not checked here.

Joe Biden, the former President, says his memoir, Promise Me, America, comes out on November 17. He says he was diagnosed with cancer while writing it, that his doctors are encouraged by how he has responded to treatment, and that he will do fewer conversations about the book.
Politics UK says the UK Government is set to ban under-16s from eBay, Vinted and Depop over fears that their messaging features let adults groom children. The post cites no source. Not checked here.

60 Minutes posts a clip of its question to President Trump about World Liberty Financial, his family's crypto company. In the interview CBS aired and published, Trump also says his deportation policy "might be too tough".

Elon Musk says he held a round table review with the Grok @Bot engineering team, that fixes go in overnight, and that users should see a dramatic improvement by tomorrow. Grok, the model that gathers this page’s posts, is made by xAI, a company in this post. Not checked here.

Fabrizio Romano posts a quote he attributes to Matheus Cunha after Manchester United conceded: "We can’t concede goals like this, we need to play like Manchester United." The quote is Romano’s report and is not checked here.
ESPN says Alycia Baumgardner beat Elif Turhan by unanimous decision to become the new IBF women’s lightweight champion. The post carries the #MVPW07 tag. Not checked here.

Mario Nawfal relays an Iraqi paper, Al-Mada, on alleged US war scenarios, including US ground forces entering Iran through Iraq. The post itself says neither is independently confirmed and there is no evidence of an invasion order. Not checked here.

Fireside Alpha posts a 46-second video and says Trump, asked about AI builders putting a 10 percent chance on AI killing humanity, said the Justice Department warned the head of a major AI company to "get ready to go to jail." The CBS transcript, as I read it, lacks that remark. Not checked here.
The Robotaxi account says robotaxi service will be available in San Antonio starting "tomorrow, 5am." The photo has no description, and the post does not say who runs the service. Not checked here.

Benny Johnson, a commentator, posts what he says Republican senators told him in calls this weekend: they are furious with Senate leadership over the SAVE Act and insider trading bills. He says a shakeup is coming. The senators are unnamed. Not checked here.
The account gtasix_ posts a 59-second video and says it is the first listen to the GTA 6 main menu theme on PS5. The video has no description here, and the claim is not checked here.
